title: Anthropic annonce les Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, données détenues par le client - Unite.AI
description: Anthropic annonce les Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, données détenues par le client  Unite.AI
bottomLine: Anthropic launches enterprise AI safeguards with customer-controlled data retention, raising stakes for secure research infrastructure adoption.
keyFindings: Anthropic introduces Enterprise Frontier Safeguards for customer data ownership and control in AI-assisted research workflows.
Data retention policies now customer-controlled, addressing regulatory and privacy concerns for institutional deployments.
Enterprise offering targets organizations seeking compliance-first AI tools for sensitive research and sensitive operations.
Move positions Anthropic as a trusted alternative to consumer AI platforms in regulated institutional environments.
whyItMatters: Belgian universities and medical centres prioritizing GDPR and data sovereignty will see this as a competitive pressure point—LeapSpace must clarify its own data governance and sovereignty guarantees to remain viable for institutions handling sensitive research data.
actionItems: Audit and document LeapSpace's data residency, retention, and deletion policies for Belgian/EU institutions; prepare comparison sheet vs. Anthropic.
Prepare use-case story showing Scopus + LeapSpace compliance advantage for medical centres handling patient-linked research metadata.
Schedule discovery calls with Vlaams universities IT/compliance leads to identify data governance concerns blocking AI workspace adoption.

title: Department of War lance ChatGPT Mil d’OpenAI sur GenAI.mil - Unite.AI
description: Department of War lance ChatGPT Mil d’OpenAI sur GenAI.mil  Unite.AI
bottomLine: U.S. Department of War deploys OpenAI's ChatGPT Mil on GenAI.mil, signalling defence sector's shift to vendor-specific AI platforms over research discovery tools.
keyFindings: U.S. military now operates ChatGPT Mil on dedicated GenAI.mil platform for defence and operational applications.
Deployment reflects government preference for narrowly-scoped, vendor-locked AI tools over broader research infrastructure.
Move suggests institutional adoption of AI assistants for non-discovery use cases: drafting, analysis, decision support.
Defence sector adoption validates market demand for domain-specific, high-security AI products; research tools face relegation.
whyItMatters: Belgian defence research institutes and EU-funded security research consortia will face pressure to adopt similar vendor-specific AI tools; ScienceDirect/Scopus/LeapSpace must differentiate on scholarly integrity, multi-source aggregation, and non-proprietary metadata to avoid commoditization in a vendor-locked market.
actionItems: Research Belgian defence research contracts (e.g., with FN Herstal, Thales, EU Common Foreign and Security Policy institutes) to identify AI procurement opportunities.
Develop messaging on how Scopus + LeapSpace enable multi-vendor AI integration without lock-in, appealing to EU defence funding governance.
Monitor EU AI Act compliance requirements for defence research; position Elsevier as a neutral, auditable alternative to vendor-specific platforms.
